decisions.rationale: The cited rule supports both five-year retention generally and thirty-year retention for special-management-substance records. The unqualified stem asks for the retention period, so choices B and E can both be legally correct depending on the record class. Narrow the stem to the general rule or explicitly exclude/scope the special-management exception.

The worker class is specific and current Article 56 directly fixes the periodic interval at once every six months. The one-month distractor is a neighboring emergency-work rule and the remaining intervals are plausible timing confusions. The item is source-bound and unambiguous.

The six-month asbestos rule is correct, but this candidate duplicates B4-C002's exact five interval choices, correct position, and reasoning pattern with only the regulated work relabeled. Under the Eisei1 collision/variation gate, reauthor the asbestos target around an asbestos-specific condition such as continuing examinations for formerly exposed current employees or another materially distinct proposition.

Current Article 40-2 item 1 directly fixes the opinion-hearing deadline at three months from the examination date or the specified substitute date. The distractors are adjacent timing rules, all five choices are explained, and the post-examination procedure is distinct from the accepted ionizing-radiation frequency item.
